name: Chrome2Rust Forensic Workstation
description: 100% pure-Rust native Win32 (WinSafe) & cross-platform Iced forensic workstation, HTTP cache inspector, CLI, and MCP server for Google Chrome.
majorCapabilities: Simple Cache & Blockfile HTTP cache inspection and extraction
Chromium User Data forensics (History, Cookies, Downloads, Logins, Extensions, Sessions, Storage)
Multi-browser non-credential forensics across Firefox, Opera (Blink & Presto), and Safari
Unified history/downloads/addons/bookmarks/autofill, search query extraction, and image EXIF + video stream carving
Offline forensic blob decryption (user-supplied keys / Linux fallback; DPAPI/OS keyring classification-only) & SHA-256/512 Merkle chain of custody
Native Win32 (WinSafe) & Iced 0.14 dual GUIs with guap-kit data grids
29-tool MCP JSON-RPC stdio server with ReadOnlyOnly default policy gate (8 legacy + 21 guap-mcp browser tools)

tools.summary: Discover local Chromium-family browsers, User Data directories, profiles, and HTTP caches.
Inspect file magic headers, container structures, missing/mismatched extensions, or directory layout to identify Chrome artifacts and cached payloads.
Scan Simple Cache / Blockfile entries matching filters and return structured JSON metadata.
Inspect headers, TLS/ALPN info, X.509 certificates, SHA-256 digest, and optional UTF-8 payload preview of a cached resource.

Extract cached payloads from Chrome cache into an output directory with decompression, extension recovery, and timestamp preservation. Writes to disk; requires --allow-mutating and confirm_destructive=true.
Run comprehensive read-only forensic analysis across Chrome User Data artifacts (history, downloads, cookies, logins, extensions, sessions, storage, findings, timeline).
Generate standalone HTML, JSON, Markdown, or bundled forensic reports from a Chrome User Data directory. Writes to disk; requires --allow-mutating and confirm_destructive=true.
Compute deterministic SHA-256 hashes and balanced Merkle root over artifacts in a Chrome User Data directory.
Carve cached images across browsers with magic-byte validation, dimension extraction, and pure-Rust TIFF/EXIF IFD + GPS metadata.
Carve cached video streams & manifests (MP4/M4S, WebM, MPEG-TS, HLS .m3u8, DASH .mpd) with 3-pass segment reassembly.
Inspect Mozilla Firefox installed add-ons, extensions, permissions, and risk flags from extensions.json/addons.json.
Inspect Mozilla Firefox bookmarks from places.sqlite and bookmarkbackups/*.jsonlz4.
Inspect Mozilla Firefox cache2/entries metadata, HTTP headers, timestamps, and payloads.
Inspect Mozilla Firefox cookies.sqlite metadata only (host, name, path, flags, expiry; cookie values omitted).
Inspect Mozilla Firefox download history from places.sqlite moz_annos.
Inspect Mozilla Firefox non-credential form autofill history from formhistory.sqlite.
Inspect Mozilla Firefox browsing history from places.sqlite.
Inspect Mozilla Firefox open and closed session tabs from sessionstore.jsonlz4 / recovery.jsonlz4.
Inspect Opera Blink (Stable/GX) and Opera Presto (dcache4.url) HTTP cache entries.
Inspect Opera Blink (History SQLite) and Opera Presto (global_history.dat / opera6.adr) browsing history.
Inspect Apple Safari bookmarks recursively from Bookmarks.plist (bplist00 or XML plist).
Inspect Apple Safari Cache.db & fsCachedData entries.
Inspect Apple Safari browsing history from History.db (CFAbsoluteTime) and History.plist.
Extract search engine queries (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo, Yandex, Baidu, YouTube, Brave, Startpage, Ecosia) from history, cache URLs/Referer headers, and sessions.
Aggregate normalized browser extensions and add-ons with permission risk flags across Chromium and Firefox.
Aggregate non-credential form autofill history from Chrome Web Data (autofill table only) and Firefox formhistory.sqlite.
Aggregate normalized bookmarks across Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Firefox, and Safari.
Aggregate normalized download histories across Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Firefox, and Safari.
Aggregate normalized browsing history across Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Firefox, and Safari.
